# Corridor scenario — JSON input template

Schema version **7** · reference bundle `2026-08-16-vessel-v2`

This is the contract for writing a scenario file by hand, for desk
research or AI-assisted data entry. A file that follows it loads without
edits.

Two failure modes, and they are not symmetric. A **wrong value** — bad
type, unknown id, out of bounds — is rejected on import, naming the
offending path. A **wrong key** is not: unknown keys are ignored in
silence, so a misspelled field imports cleanly and is simply dropped.
Rule 5 is about that, and it is the one to be careful of.

## The five rules

1. **Keep every key; write `null`, never omit.** Behaviour verified
   against the importer: a missing *scalar* is rejected outright (even a
   nullable override — `null` and absent are NOT the same to the
   validator), while a missing optional *block* such as `financing` is
   accepted and read as "module off". Do not rely on that distinction:
   copy the whole template.
2. **`null` means "use the model's own value"** — the benchmark, the
   derived figure, or "module off". It does NOT mean zero. Writing `0`
   where you meant "leave it alone" charges a real zero and changes the
   result.
3. **Only fill a field you have a source for.** Every non-null number is
   an OVERRIDE: it replaces a benchmark the model would otherwise derive,
   and the UI marks it so a reader can see what you asserted.
4. **Id strings must come from the lists below.** An unrecognised
   `fuelId`, `typeId` or `countryId` is a hard error — the model never
   falls back to a default for an id it does not know.
5. **An unknown key is SILENTLY IGNORED — this is the dangerous one.**
   Misspell a field (`oneWayDistanceNM`, `capexUsdM`) and the file still
   imports; your value is dropped and the model quietly uses its own.
   Nothing warns you. Check every number you meant to set actually shows
   an OVERRIDE badge in the UI before trusting the result.

## What you must NOT do

| Don't | Why |
|---|---|
| Set `schemaVersion` to anything else | It pins the shape. A LOWER number is migrated on load (your file is reinterpreted); a higher one is rejected. |
| Change `refBundleId` | It pins the reference data (vessel table, fuels, countries). Bundles are immutable; an unknown id is an error. |
| Use `0` to mean "no override" | `0` is a real value. Use `null`. |
| Fill both a price override and production CAPEX/OPEX on a `purchase` side | Purchase forces production lines to zero — the CAPEX you wrote is discarded, which looks like a bug. |
| Override one side's `fuelTonnesPerVesselYear` alone | The two sides then carry different delivered energy, and CO₂ abated compares unequal transport work. The model raises an amber note; fix the pairing or state why. |
| Hand-write `buildHere` | It is written by the map when you evaluate a site. Leave the whole block null unless you are round-tripping a file that already had one. |
| Put a fleet total in `capexUsdMPerShip` | It is PER SHIP; the model multiplies by `cargo.vessels`. A fleet number here is silently ×N too large. |

## Units and bounds

Getting a unit wrong is the most common way a researched scenario comes
out wrong while still importing cleanly. The model cannot detect it.

| Field | Unit | Bounds |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo.oneWayDistanceNm` | nautical miles, **one way** | > 0 |
| `cargo.roundtripsPerYear` | roundtrips per vessel per year | > 0 |
| `cargo.vessels` | ships | integer > 0 |
| `cargo.unitsPerYear` | cargo units per year (`unit` says which) | ≥ 0 |
| `cargo.startYear` | calendar year | 2000–2100 |
| `cargo.horizonYears` | years modelled | 1–40 |
| `cargo.inflation`, `cargo.waccOverride` | **fraction**, not percent (0.02 = 2%) | finite |
| `vessel.*.capexUsdMPerShip` | USD million, **per ship** | ≥ 0 |
| `vessel.*.opexUsdMPerShipPerYear` | USD million per year, **per ship** | ≥ 0 |
| `*.overrides.priceUsdPerTonne` | USD per tonne of fuel | ≥ 0 |
| `*.overrides.fuelTonnesPerVesselYear` | tonnes per **vessel** per year | ≥ 0 |
| `*.overrides.lhvMjPerTonne` | MJ per tonne | > 0 |
| `*.overrides.combustionEfTco2PerTonne` | tCO₂ per tonne of fuel | ≥ 0 |
| `*.overrides.wtwGco2PerMj` | gCO₂e per MJ | ≥ 0 |
| `*.overrides.prod*/portStorage*/barge*UsdM` | USD million (CAPEX) or USD million/year (OPEX) | ≥ 0 |
| `*.emissions.pilotShare` | fraction of energy | 0–1 |
| `*.emissions.certifiedWttGco2ePerMj` | gCO₂e per MJ, well-to-**tank** | > 0 |
| `regulation.eurUsd` | USD per EUR | > 0 |
| `regulation.ets.euaEurPerTonne` | EUR per tonne CO₂ | ≥ 0 |
| `regulation.*.scope` | fraction of the voyage in scope | 0–1 |
| `financing.*Rate`, `debtShare`, `*Support` | fraction | 0–1 |

## What the model derives — do not research these

Leave these `null`. The model computes them, and an override replaces a
figure that is consistent with the rest of the scenario with one that may
not be.

- **Fuel consumption** (`*.overrides.fuelTonnesPerVesselYear`) —
  `2 × oneWayDistanceNm × roundtripsPerYear × GJ/nm × 1000 ÷ LHV`. Set it
  only to reproduce a published burn, and set **both sides** if you set
  either, or the energy-parity check will flag the mismatch.
- **Vessel CAPEX/OPEX** — the benchmark is the vessel type's figure, and
  for the green side × (1 + the fuel's readiness premium).
- **Emission factors** (`combustionEfTco2PerTonne`, `lhvMjPerTonne`,
  `wtwGco2PerMj`) — derived from the fuel-emissions dataset. Override only
  with a certified pathway value you can cite.
- **Fossil port/vessel CAPEX** — 0 by rule (existing infrastructure).
  Override only when the comparison genuinely builds new fossil assets.

## Minimum viable scenario

The smallest set of decisions that produces a meaningful result. Everything
else can stay on its benchmark:

1. `cargo`: `countryId`, `oneWayDistanceNm`, `startYear`, `horizonYears`,
   `unitsPerYear`, `vessels`, `roundtripsPerYear`
2. `vessel.typeId`
3. `green.fuelId` + `green.sourcing`, `fossil.fuelId` + `fossil.sourcing`
4. `regulation`: switch on the schemes that apply (`enabled: true`)

With those set and everything else `null`, the model derives consumption
from the geometry, prices fuel from the bundle, and costs vessels from the
type — a complete, internally consistent scenario.

## Checking your file before you rely on it

1. Import it. A rejected file names the offending path — fix that path,
   do not delete the field.
2. Look for **OVERRIDE badges**. Every one is something you asserted. If
   you did not mean to assert it, set it back to `null`.
3. Check the **energy-parity note** on the Results Energy card. If it is
   showing, your two fuel burns describe different amounts of transport
   work and the CO₂-abated figure is comparing unlike with unlike.
4. Sanity-check the derived fuel burn against the vessel: a Handymax on a
   9,500 nm corridor at 3 roundtrips burns ~4,500 t of LSFO a year. If
   your figure is far off, the distance or roundtrip count is likely wrong.
